editorial:
Ever felt like you were just pretending to be normal while everyone else had a secret manual for life? That is exactly where you find yourself with the main character here. He has spent his whole life feeling like an outsider, wearing a fake smile just to fit in. The movie captures that lonely feeling of being in a room full of people but still feeling completely alone. It is a heavy story that looks at how hard it is when society just ignores you or treats you like a joke, pushing you further into a dark hole.

The acting is raw and really makes you feel the weight of his sadness. While the pacing is slow and can feel a bit gloomy, it works because it puts you right in his headspace. If you like deep character studies that do not sugarcoat the truth, you will appreciate this. To get the best experience, you should definitely look for the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night in. It is a tough watch, but it hits home if you have ever felt misunderstood.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the main character reaches his breaking point after years of hiding his true self. He stops trying to fit in and accepts that he cannot find a place in a world that rejects him. The movie ends on a very sad note as he follows through with his plan to end his life. There is no magic fix or happy twist, just a quiet and honest look at a life lost to loneliness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about mental health and feeling like an outcast.
